title: Why DLP did or did not fire: pipeline position, evaluation mode and exemptions
aliases: cloud apps and url exceptions for dlp

prose.text: Three separate things decide whether a DLP rule gets a say, in this order: whether DLP is reached, which evaluation mode the tenant uses, and what is exempted.

prose.label: Is DLP reached?
prose.text: {{dlp-after-url-and-file-type}} {{earlier-block-skips-dlp}} Earlier policies are in [[zia.url-filtering]] and [[zia.cloud-app-control.precedence]]. {{decrypt-dependency}} {{scope-bounded-by-decryption}} The decrypt side is in [[zia.ssl-inspection.pipeline]]. Whether this is the most common cause is open {{gap:ssl-bypass-most-common-cause}}.

prose.label: Which mode?
prose.text: {{evaluate-all-default-vs-mode}} {{evaluate-all-switch}} The API shape of sub-rules is in [[zia.dlp.rule-wire-shape]]. {{exception-rules}}

Size, archive and text limits that stop inspection of a file that was reached are in [[zia.dlp.inspection-limits]]; timeouts on large uploads are open [[zia.dlp.inspection-limits:large-upload-timeout]]. Rule criteria are in [[zia.dlp.rules]].

checks.do: Whether the tenant evaluates rules in order to the first match or evaluates all rules, read from webDlpGlobalOptions before assuming first match.
Whether rules written for one evaluation mode still give the same result after the other mode is enabled.

dlp-after-url-and-file-type.statement: For a POST request the Public Service Edge applies policies in a listed order in which Cloud App Control, URL Filtering, Malware Protection and File Type Control all come before Data Loss Prevention.

evidence.after: The Public Service Edge scans the POST request and applies policies in the following order:
quotes: Cloud App Control: The Public Service Edge checks if the requested application violates the Cloud App Control policy configured by your organization.
URL Filtering: The Public Service Edge checks if the requested URL belongs to URL categories or custom URL categories blocked by your organization's URL Filtering policy.
Malware Protection: The Public Service Edge checks files in the request against anti-virus and anti-spyware signatures.
File Type Control: The Public Service Edge checks if the POST request violates your File Type Control policy.
Data Loss Prevention: The Public Service Edge checks if the POST request includes content that violates your organization's DLP policy.
2. Cloud App Control:
3. URL Filtering:

earlier-block-skips-dlp.statement: If an earlier policy blocks the transaction, the DLP policy is never triggered and no DLP notification is sent. The vendor's example is a PDF containing credit card numbers blocked by File Type Control, so the auditor is never told about attempted Social Security number exfiltration.

quotes: Under the File Type Control policy, the organization blocks PDFs from being sent out of its corporate network.

Under the DLP policy, the organization blocks documents containing US Social Security numbers and specifies that the Zscaler service send notifications to auditors when it detects users attempting to do so.

If a user in this organization attempts to send a PDF that contains credit card numbers, the service blocks the transaction, but it does so because of the File Type Control policy, rather than the DLP policy.
The DLP policy itself is never triggered, and the service does not send a notification alerting the auditor that a user has attempted to send Social Security numbers out of the organization.

decrypt-dependency.statement: Payload-based checks, DLP among them, do not run on traffic that SSL inspection does not decrypt, so an SSL inspection bypass upstream silently removes DLP for that traffic.
decrypt-dependency.conditions: Follows from the SSL inspection subject's reading of the documented no-inspection path; this subject adds no new source.

scope-bounded-by-decryption.statement: A DLP rule cannot reach traffic that SSL inspection does not decrypt, so its effective scope is the decrypted subset regardless of its own criteria.
scope-bounded-by-decryption.conditions: Inference from the decrypt dependency; no source states it for DLP scope directly.

evaluate-all-default-vs-mode.statement: By default DLP rules are evaluated in rule order and evaluation stops at the first match. In Evaluate All Rules mode (enabled through the Zscaler account team) the service evaluates all rules and enforces the rule with the most restrictive action; rule order decides only among matched rules with the same action.

quotes: This article applies only to organizations with Evaluate All Rules mode enabled. To access this feature, contact your Zscaler Account team.
By default, the Zscaler service evaluates inline Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy rules according to rule order, with evaluation stopping at the first match.
you can instead have the Zscaler service evaluate all rules, enforcing the rule with the most restrictive action.
Evaluate All Rules mode uses rule order only when multiple rules with the same action are matched.

evaluate-all-switch.statement: The mode is set on the DLP Advanced Settings page, and all existing inline DLP rules must be deleted before the evaluation method is changed. The API exposes it as the `enableEvaluateAllDlpRules` flag of the `webDlpGlobalOptions` resource.

quotes: With Evaluate All Rules mode enabled for your organization, you first set how the Zscaler service evaluates inline DLP rules on the DLP Advanced Settings page
You must first delete all existing inline DLP rules before you change the way the Zscaler service evaluates rules.
webDlpGlobalOptionsEndpoint = "/zia/api/v1/webDlpGlobalOptions"
EnableEvaluateAllDlpRules   bool                      `json:"enableEvaluateAllDlpRules,omitempty"`

exception-rules.statement: In Evaluate All Rules mode an admin can add exception rules, child rules that exclude specific users or groups from a parent rule, with no limit on how many a parent can have. The API accepts exception rules only when the tenant's inline DLP evaluation is set to evaluate all rules.

quotes: you have the ability to create exception rules, which are child rules that allow you to exclude specific users or groups in your organization
There is not a limit to the number of exception rules that you can assign to each parent rule.
// Note: Exception rules can be configured only when the inline DLP rule evaluation type is set to evaluate all DLP rules in the DLP Advanced Settings.

exemption-list.statement: To exempt a specific website, custom URL category or cloud application from DLP evaluation, add it to the Cloud Apps & URL Exceptions for DLP list.

evidence.after: You then configure your policy rules based on that setting:
quotes: If you want to exempt a specific website or custom URL category from DLP evaluation, you must add the website or URL category to the Cloud Apps & URL Exceptions for DLP list.
If you want to exempt a specific cloud application from DLP evaluation, you must add the cloud application to the Cloud Apps & URL Exceptions for DLP list.

ssl-bypass-most-common-cause.title: Unverified legacy statement: an SSL inspection bypass is the single most common cause of DLP not firing
ssl-bypass-most-common-cause.blocks: ranking causes of a missed DLP detection
ssl-bypass-most-common-cause.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "The single most common 'DLP didn't fire' cause is an SSL Inspection bypass upstream." No registered source ranks causes; the decrypt dependency itself is held in decrypt-dependency.

evaluate-all-semantic-detail.title: Whether Evaluate All Rules logs every matched rule and how exception rules interact with parent actions
evaluate-all-semantic-detail.blocks: explaining which rules appear in logs when several match, and how a matched exception rule changes a parent rule's action
evaluate-all-semantic-detail.detail: The help states the most restrictive action is enforced and that exception rules exclude users or groups. Unverified legacy statement: "Evaluate All Rules ... is an alternative mode that runs every DLP rule against every request ... when you want to log ALL DLP violations for audit purposes." Logging of non-enforced matches is not stated by any registered source.

pipeline-terminal-tier.title: Unverified legacy statement: DLP sits in the terminal tier of the full-URL pass with Sandbox, Malware, File Type Control and IPS content checks
pipeline-terminal-tier.blocks: saying all those checks share one tier
pipeline-terminal-tier.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "DLP is in the terminal tier of the full-URL pass alongside Sandbox, Malware, File Type Control, and IPS content checks." The captured enforcement order lists these as separate numbered steps with DLP after File Type Control (see dlp-after-url-and-file-type); the 'tier' grouping is not stated.
